verdict.probe_answer: Both arms make the watchdog select arm active only when watchdog config exists and use a Pending future plus no spawned task when disabled. Both also use Task-4 activity tracking, so unmodeled updates can keep an active turn alive. Arm B is stronger because its tests actually run active and unmodeled turns for longer than the idle timeout, which proves the watchdog is not firing on live activity; Arm A's active/unmodeled test total duration is under the 100ms idle threshold, so it would pass even if activity did not refresh the idle deadline.
verdict.rationale: Both implementations follow the key binding points: spawn only when configured, use tokio Instant::from_std, undo the last-activity +1 sentinel with saturating_sub(1), discard the watchdog cancel inner outcome and return Err(()) with timed_out_local, drop the watchdog completion sender on driver exit, and map watchdog Err(()) to AgentTimedOut. Arm B's implementation is at least as correct and its coverage materially better: it explicitly exercises modeled and unmodeled streams beyond idle_timeout, while Arm A's three 20ms delays keep the whole turn below idle_timeout and do not validate the requirement that ongoing activity prevents timeout. That is a real requirement-coverage gap a reviewer would ask Arm A to fix. Arm B adds comments and a helper, but this remains scoped to the requested
